issues.description: SR3 has no mutant that specifically targets it and is detected only by it; validation report shows SR3 as an uncovered requirement (0/1 mutants detected). This means the SR3 check's discriminative power against a plausible spurious-finding-on-WDT_CTRL/WDT_TIMEOUT mutant is unverified, even though the logic appears present in check_sr3().
Mutation score is 0.857 (6/7) rather than 1.0 solely due to the SR3 gap; all other requirements (FR1-FR4, SR1, SR2) are well covered and discriminative per the mutation analysis.

recommendations: Investigate and fix the SR3 mutant detection gap: verify that the sr3_spurious_finding_on_wdt_ctrl (or equivalent) mutant used in mutation testing actually triggers the finding_mischaracterizes_documented_behavior or finding_claims_hidden_logic paths in check_sr3; the current keyword/phrase matching may not align with the actual mutant's wording.

Add a unit-level example finding (e.g. one that claims 'hidden trigger logic in WDT_CTRL bit1 toggle sequence') to a test fixture to confirm check_sr3 flags it as expected before relying on mutation testing alone.
Consider tightening or broadening DOCUMENTED_BEHAVIOR_PHRASES/CLAIM_KEYWORDS in check_sr3 if the mutation harness's injected finding text does not match current keyword sets.

requirement_results.evidence: golden_run: exit_code 0, status pass, all FR1-FR4/SR1-SR3 PASS lines emitted
vulnerable_run: exit_code 1, status fail, FR1 fails on empty findings and cascades correctly to FR2-FR4/SR1-SR3 FAIL with clear reasons
requirement_results.requirement: Shipped naive baseline (empty findings, reset_req_reliable=true) must FAIL

requirement_results.evidence: check_fr1/fr2/fr3/fr4 in evaluate.py implement concrete structural and content checks tied to the pinned interface fields (findings[], summary, reset_req_reliable, severity)
requirement_results.requirement: FR1-FR4 functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable via schema/content checks

requirement_results.evidence: check_sr1 verifies exact magic constant 0xDEADC0DE derived structurally from RTL plus reload-effect description; check_sr2 checks reset_req_reliable==false and no mischaracterization of WDT_PET; check_sr3 scans for spurious findings on WDT_CTRL/WDT_TIMEOUT
requirement_results.requirement: SR1-SR3 security requirements are checked separately from FR and are substantively distinct

requirement_results.evidence: SR1 includes optional iverilog/vvp corroboration via tb_wdt_trojan_check.v that injects the reported magic value and checks reset_req behavior at expected timeout, reinforcing the textual check
requirement_results.requirement: Security-relevant behavior (trojan trigger) is actively verifiable, not just pattern-matched superficially

requirement_results.evidence: README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, register_map.md, and wdt_top.v comments describe WDT_CFG_ALIAS as a 'legacy config passthrough / scratch register' with no explicit mention of trojan/backdoor/CWE ids; the magic constant 0xDEADC0DE only appears in the RTL logic itself, not narrated as malicious
requirement_results.requirement: Public artifacts do not leak hidden CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit statements that the design is intentionally trojaned

requirement_results.evidence: wdt_top.v's int_pet_shadow signal matches ground_truth description exactly (addr 0x0C, data 32'hDEADC0DE, ORed into reload_strobe); register_map.md and design_brief.md consistently describe 0x0C as having no functional effect, matching the intended stealthy trojan framing
requirement_results.requirement: Coherence between public inputs, hidden ground truth, and expected outputs

requirement_results.evidence: validation report flags SR3 as an uncovered_requirement with 0 mutants detected out of 1 targeting mutant, indicating the SR3-targeting mutant (e.g. sr3_spurious_finding_on_wdt_ctrl) was not actually caught by check_sr3 in the mutation run, despite the check's logic appearing plausible on inspection
requirement_results.requirement: SR3 detection is empirically validated via mutation testing
